definitions.explanation: Lacking generosity of spirit; unable to accept different opinions or forgive minor faults.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{心|こころ}が{狭|せま}い。
そんな{小|ちい}さなことで{怒|おこ}るなんて、{心|こころ}が{狭|せま}いよ。
examples.english: Getting angry over such a small thing — you're being petty.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}とは{違|ちが}う{意見|いけん}を{受|う}け{入|い}れられないのは、{心|こころ}が{狭|せま}い{証拠|しょうこ}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think being unable to accept opinions different from your own is a sign of narrow-mindedness.

notes:
Literally "the heart is narrow." This expression describes someone who is petty, intolerant, or lacks generosity of spirit. It is a direct criticism of character and is considered fairly blunt.

The expression is the antonym of {心|こころ}が{広|ひろ}い (broad-minded, generous). Japanese has many idiomatic expressions using {心|こころ} to describe personality traits.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {心|こころ}が{狭|せま}い{人|ひと}: a petty person
- {心|こころ}の{狭|せま}さ: narrow-mindedness (nominalized form)

RELATED WORDS:
- {心|こころ}が{広|ひろ}い: broad-minded, generous — the direct antonym
- {器|うつわ}が{小|ちい}さい: small-hearted, petty — similar meaning, emphasizes limited capacity as a person
- {寛大|かんだい}: tolerant, magnanimous — formal antonym describing generosity of spirit
- {狭量|きょうりょう}: narrow-minded — formal, written equivalent
